ops.text: `task build` silently breaks `capt-hook pack test plugin`, and the failure mode gives you nothing to work with. Taskfile.yml:30 runs `ln -sf ../../bin/ccx plugin/bin/ccx`, repointing the tracked symlink (committed value: `../scripts/install-binary.sh`) at the local dev build. After that, every `capt-hook pack test plugin` dies with the bare line `binrun: run version command: signal: killed` — no mention of which binary, which version, or that a symlink is involved. `pack test` had worked minutes earlier in the same session; the only thing that changed was that a `task build` ran. I burned five attempts on it: disabling the Bash sandbox (not the cause), copying `plugin/` to /tmp and re-pointing the symlink at `../scripts/install-binary.sh` (times out — the installer tries to fetch), and pointing it at the installed release binary (still killed, because `plugin/bin/ccx.binrun` pins v0.34.0 while the installed release is v0.33.0). What finally worked: copy `plugin/` aside, delete BOTH `bin/ccx` and `bin/ccx.binrun`, and drop a real binary in at `plugin/bin/ccx` — then 608 tests run fine. Two fixes worth considering: have `pack test` say which path and version it failed to resolve instead of `signal: killed`, and/or have `task build` not clobber a tracked symlink (a `bin/ccx.local` + gitignore, or a separate `task build:dev`). Also note the trap for whoever hits this next: `capt-hook --hooks <dir>` does NOT override an installed plugin pack, so patching a copy elsewhere and re-running silently verifies the *unpatched* code — I confirmed that with a sentinel string that never appeared in the output.
